steps.title: Fetching the issue through the Jira MCP server

detail.description: Users should be able to log into the web application using valid credentials.

jira_issue.description: Users should be able to log into the web application using valid credentials.

analysis.business_objective: Let registered users reach the product catalogue by signing in with valid credentials.

requirements.description: The login page accepts a username.
The login page accepts a password.
A Login action submits the entered credentials for authentication.
Successful authentication lands the user on the Products page.

acceptance_criteria.description: Successful authentication displays the Products page.

dependencies.name: Authentication service
dependencies.description: Validates credentials and starts the session.

dependencies.name: Test user accounts
dependencies.description: At least one active account with known credentials.

dependencies.name: Web application environment
dependencies.description: A reachable deployment that serves the login and Products pages.

risks.description: Login gates every other user journey, so a regression here blocks all downstream testing.
Test credentials may leak if they are stored in plain text in the automation repo.
No acceptance criteria cover failed logins, so negative behaviour is untested by default.

ambiguities.description: 'Valid credentials' is not defined: account types, locked users and MFA are not mentioned.
ambiguities.impact: Test data and the happy-path scope could change if MFA or multiple roles apply.

ambiguities.description: The expected behaviour for invalid credentials is not specified.
ambiguities.impact: Negative tests would rely on assumed error messages.

testing_scope.reason: Core behaviour is defined by four acceptance criteria.
All criteria are exercised through the browser login page.
Login is the entry point for every journey.
A broken login invalidates the rest of the suite.
Invalid-credential behaviour is a known gap in the ticket.

automation_assessment.reason: The happy path is deterministic and every step is exposed in the browser.
automation_candidates: Successful login with a valid account
automation_constraints: Needs a stable, non-MFA test account
Negative scenarios wait on confirmed error messages

required_agents.reason: Several testing types apply and one ambiguity needs a plan.

assumptions.description: Test accounts are pre-provisioned and active.
The test environment has MFA disabled.

analysis.analysis_summary: A small, well-bounded login story. The happy path is ready to automate now. Failed-login behaviour and MFA need a decision before negative tests can be written.

review.message: Review the analysis before the strategy agent runs.

strategy.strategy_summary: Automate the login happy path in the browser first, run it as a smoke and regression check, and hold negative scenarios until the error behaviour is confirmed.

testing_types.reason: Every step happens on the login page.
Fast gate before wider suites run.

manual_scope: Exploratory pass on error messages once they are defined
Visual check of the login page
test_data_requirements: One active, non-MFA user with known credentials held in a secret store
risks: Regression in login blocks all journeys
Credential leakage from the automation repo
strategy.automation_approach: Playwright with TypeScript, Page Object Model, credentials read from environment variables, tagged @smoke and @regression.
assumptions: Test accounts are pre-provisioned and active
open_questions: Is MFA enabled in any test environment?
What message is shown for invalid credentials?
